_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY. Every value that looks like a credential is a placeholder.
Copy this to gateway.json, fill in the four REPLACE_ME fields, and read
README.md for where the real values live. JSON has no comments, so this
key is the note; the parser ignores unknown keys.
Paths are container paths. /config is the bind mount.
port: FIXED, deliberately. Omitting it binds an ephemeral port and the
panels come up unable to find the gateway on a boot that reported no
error (gateway_config.dart, serverConfigFromJson). Say 0 only if an
ephemeral port is what you mean.
9443 and not 8443: on the SVN rig 8443 is already published by
docker-update. Whatever you pick here must match GATEWAY_PORT in
docker-compose.yml — compose cannot read this file.
publisher_id: what this gateway calls itself on the wire and in
pg_stat_activity. One per gateway on a plant LAN.
PATHS, never bytes — TlsConfig cannot hold key material by design.
Mint these with relay_certs; see README 'Mint the certificates'.
Delete this whole block to serve plaintext ws:// — the gateway logs a
loud ERROR line at bind when you do, and means it.
The token file maps a panel's token to its identity:
{"tokens": {"<token>": {"stationId": "...",
"role": "view"|"operate"}}}
It must be mode 0600 and owned by uid 1000 — FileTokenValidator
refuses to load one any group or other can read. Delete this block
and EVERY peer that can reach the port gets operate rights.

_links_comment: One entry per PLC. `alias` is the link's NAME: it owns the
PIPE.upstream.<alias>.* health keys and is what a status notification
reports — it must be unique, and the gateway refuses to start if two
links share one.
`answers_to` is WHICH keymapping server_alias this link serves, and it
is a separate fact from the name. Omit it and the link answers to its
own alias — right for a plant whose integrator named the servers. Set
it to null (or "") for the unnamed server: the live plant file carries
"server_alias": null on every OPC UA entry, and without this field
every one of those keys is unroutable — errorConfig (q=770) on every
panel, with the session connected and nothing in the log. That is not
hypothetical; it is what the first rig deployment did
(RIG-TEST-FINDINGS.md F1).
protocol: opcua | modbus | umas | m2400.
Credentials: NOT one pair or the other. The two do different jobs and a
hardened server needs BOTH.
certificate_path + private_key_path select the SECURE CHANNEL. The
gateway asks for SIGNANDENCRYPT only when a certificate is present,
and for NONE when it is not (gateway_config.dart, _opcUaClient).
username + password are the USER TOKEN, passed independently.
So a server that offers no None endpoint — this plant's, and any
hardened one — REJECTS a username-only config, with:
error/client  No suitable endpoint found
error/client  SecureChannel must be connected to send request  (once a
second, for ever)
That message names neither credentials nor security mode. Adding the
certificate is the fix. Giving neither is an anonymous, unencrypted
session, which only a server offering a None endpoint will accept.
The certificate and key are DER, not PEM — see README 'Convert the OPC UA
credentials to DER'.
An empty list is legal and serves nothing but the PIPE.* health keys —
useful for a first boot that only has to prove the port answers.

_comment: All four credential fields together — this is the combination that
connects to the SVN plant. Dropping the certificate pair drops the
channel to NONE and the server refuses it.
A second link, shown for the shape only. Delete it if the plant has
one PLC. `unit_id` is Modbus-only.
Certificate WITHOUT username is a legitimate combination — an
encrypted channel with an anonymous user token — but only if the
server admits anonymous users. Most do not.

_key_mappings_comment: REQUIRED. The plant's key -> node mapping, in KeyMappings shape:
Export it from the running HMI's preferences (the `key_mappings` row) or
reuse the file the backend already reads. {"nodes": {}} is a valid empty

_comment: History. Omit this whole block, or set enabled:false, and the gateway
opens no database connection at all.
table_prefix: KEEP 'gw_' while the app's collector is still running.
The two writers pick byte-identical table names otherwise, the tables
have no primary key, and the row count silently doubles while the two
retention policies uninstall each other. Emptying it is refused unless
sole_writer is also true — a deliberate two-field act, after the app's
collector has been stopped.
ssl_mode: disable | require | verifyFull. The rig's Postgres is
configured ssl=on, so 'require' is the right answer there.
